Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 23-year-old woman with acute, progressively worsening lower abdominal pain, light inter-menstrual bleeding, mild nausea, recent constipation, Implanon in situ, last pregnancy test 1 month ago. No fever, urinary symptoms, or shoulder pain.

Working diagnosis: Pelvic pain of uncertain etiology—rule out ectopic pregnancy.

Relevant differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx):
• Ectopic pregnancy (High likelihood)—pain, abnormal bleeding, contraceptive failure possible, last pregnancy test outdated.  
• Pelvic inflammatory disease (Moderate)—pain, bleeding, discharge; absence of fever lowers probability.  
• Ovarian torsion or hemorrhagic cyst (Moderate)—constant severe pain with light bleeding possible.

Management priorities: urgent confirmation of pregnancy status, prompt in-person abdominal and pelvic examination, safety-net advice.

Management Plan

- Arrange face-to-face appointment for full abdominal and pelvic examination as soon as possible (patient to call support line to book).  
- Patient to perform urine pregnancy test today; instructed to call immediately if positive.  
- Safety-net: seek urgent care if pain intensifies, vomiting/fever develops, or unable to tolerate fluids.  
- No medications prescribed during tele-visit.  
- Education provided regarding seriousness of possible ectopic pregnancy and need for prompt review.

1. Ectopic pregnancy – High likelihood: acute pelvic pain + light bleeding; contraceptive failure possible; needs exclusion urgently.  
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease – Moderate likelihood: lower abdominal pain, bleeding/discharge, sexually active.  
3. Ovarian torsion / hemorrhagic ovarian cyst – Moderate likelihood: severe constant pelvic pain, reproductive age female.
